title: What If Every Outdoor Light on Earth Switched Off?

scenes.text: What if every outdoor light on Earth switched off tonight? Animals would notice first.
More than eighty percent of people live under light-polluted skies, and one in three can't see the Milky Way.
Migrating songbirds, which circle brightly lit buildings all night until they're exhausted, would stop being lured in.
Sea turtle hatchlings that now crawl toward roads and buildings would head for the ocean again.
After one power plant dimmed its lights in 2013, ten snowy plover nests appeared on a beach where none had nested before.
Light pollution is growing about two percent a year. One dark night would show what we've been hiding from the sky.

description:
What if every outdoor light on Earth switched off?
Over 80 percent of people live under light-polluted skies, and the wildlife pays for it: lost hatchlings, circling songbirds, silent fireflies.
